summary: Tsutomu Kubo was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912) under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate at Tohoku University (by 1953). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, and Toyo University.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a special appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies in 2017.

Tu Weiming works in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard universities under scholars including Zongsan Mou, he held faculty posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard, and Peking University.

Tubten Chokyi Dorje was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Dilgo Khyentse and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Tubten Nyendrak was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. His students included Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and later taught Steven Neal Weinberger.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.
Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Halle until 1912. He held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Tulku Sherdor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia under Ted Norton and Jeffrey Hopkins, and trained traditionally under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and later served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Samten Gyatso, Dilgo Khyentse, and the 16th Karmapa, among others. He founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery and taught numerous students.

Turrell V. Wylie was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Washington, he studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche, and spent his academic career teaching at the University of Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute (attested 2008 and 2019) and trained under Acharya Tashi Wangchuk (2003–2004) and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (attested 2019).

Tzungkuen Wen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Queensland in 2009 under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He also served as a lecturer at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005.

Tōru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He held faculty appointments at Kyushu University and Kyoto University.

U Ba Khin was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Saya Thetgyi (~1937–1945). He founded the International Meditation Centre and taught students including S. N. Goenka and Mother Sayamagyi.

Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.
